children: U.S. diesel prices have surged to a record, adding to cost pressures for freight, agriculture, and other diesel-intensive businesses as higher energy prices threaten to keep inflation elevated.
Diesel prices reached $6.40 a gallon, up more than 88% over nine months, according to The Kobeissi Letter. Truck drivers were paying about $3 more per gallon than they were in January, the post said.

The rise has broader implications because diesel is widely used in trucking, agriculture, construction, and other industrial activities. Higher fuel costs can feed into transportation and operating expenses, with some of those costs eventually passed on to customers.
The national average reached $6.0556 a gallon,
to the American Automobile Association. In California, prices were approaching $8 a gallon.
The surge in prices raised concerns about renewed energy-driven inflation just ahead of the fuel’s peak-demand season.
The Kobeissi Letter also put the average U.S. gasoline price at $4.44 a gallon, about 13% away from a new record high.

The jump in fuel costs comes as markets assess the inflationary impact of higher energy prices. Rising diesel prices are particularly important for businesses exposed to freight and logistics costs, while sustained energy inflation could complicate the outlook for interest rates.
The Kobeissi Letter said market expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate hikes were rising.
Fuel costs are climbing as crude oil prices surge following a sharp escalation in fighting between the U.S. and Iran this month. U.S. crude futures (
) topped $100 a barrel last week for the first time since May and are up roughly 20% in September.

title: Diesel prices hit record as fuel costs add to inflation pressure
